description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to Use Class C4 (HMO-house in multiple occupation) with associated amenity, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:00 Existing floor plans, 00a Existing elevations and sections, 01 Proposed plan and elevations, 01a Proposed floor plans, 01b Proposed elevations and sections, 02 Proposed storage, 03 Proposed storage, 04 Proposed site plans and gate, 05 Location Plan, 07 Proposed Block Plan, BNG statement, Planning Fire Safety Strategy, Planning Fire Safety Plan, SuDS proforma, CIL form, Highway Safety Impact Form, Planning Statement.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than five residents at any one time without first obtaining the approval, in writing, of the Local Planning Authority.     Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not adversely affect the adjoining

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

No cooking facilities, including hot plates, shall be installed in the bedrooms of the development hereby permitted unless details have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Any cooking facilities shall thereafter only be implemented in accordance with the details that have been approved pursuant to this condition. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details of the 5 long stay cycle parking spaces have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The dedicated cycle store providing a minimum of 5 long stay parking spaces shall fulfil the following, to the satisfaction of the Responsible Authority:-	Location: Near entrances or main access-	Design: Stands or wall bars-	Security: Secure, overlooked, well-lit.-	Coverage: Covered and enclosed where possible.-	Accessibility: Step-free, no obstructions, with a minimum width of at least 1.2 metres with no obstructions. The cycle parking spaces shall be fully constructed in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the means of enclosure for pedestrians, and cyclists have been approved in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure a safe, secure, and accessible environment for all users of the development, including pedestrians and cyclists, and to maintain the visual quality and functionality of the site.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

The development shall not commence until details of source control SuDS has been submitted and approved by the Local Authority. Source control SuDS measures include green roofs, rain gardens and permeable paving. The details must include plans, specifications and maintenance information. The developer should use the SuDS Proforma for minor developers found on our webpage https://www.enfield.gov.uk/services/planning/sustainable-drainage-systems to assist them through our requirements.REASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

No car parking is permitted within the development site as submitted as there is no dropped kerb and safe means of access. Reason: To control the level of parking on the site and to safeguard the uses of other areas
